title: Project Overview
description: Begin with the README for the project's local-first purpose: turn business questions into safe, auditable SQLite queries. It also maps the configuration, model, workflow, safety, interface, and operational pieces that the rest of this tour follows.

title: Windows Launcher
description: For Windows users, the launcher checks for uv and starts the application through the project's locked environment. It is the most direct operational handoff from the setup guidance into the user-facing runtime.
languageLesson: A Windows command launcher is deliberately thin: it delegates dependency resolution and process execution to uv so the application environment stays consistent with development and CI.

title: Command-Line Entry
description: The CLI is the primary programmatic entry point for asking questions, inspecting resolved settings, launching Streamlit, and running evaluations. Its dependency path leads into the agent, settings, provider, auditing, and evaluation layers without coupling callers to their implementation details.

title: Interactive Interface
description: The Streamlit application provides the conversational path alongside the CLI: it collects configuration, chooses a database, builds the agent, streams progress, and displays results. Reading it after the CLI makes clear that both interfaces reuse the same governed execution core.

title: Validated Settings
description: Runtime settings normalize provider credentials, database limits, and environment inputs before any model or database action occurs. This shared foundation gives the CLI and UI from the previous steps a single, validated configuration contract.
languageLesson: Typed Python settings move environment parsing and validation to the boundary, preventing invalid configuration from becoming a late workflow failure.

title: Provider Catalog
description: The model factory encapsulates provider-specific construction and curated model discovery for local Ollama plus Hugging Face, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and xAI. Keeping this catalog behind one factory lets the workflow depend on a chat-model capability rather than on any provider SDK.

title: Agent Workflow
description: The LangGraph workflow turns a question into an answer through schema discovery, SQL drafting, safety checks, execution, repair, summarization, and auditing. It is the central coordinator that connects the interfaces, settings, providers, prompts, database, and guardrail layers introduced so far.

title: SQL Safety Boundary
description: Generated SQL is parsed and validated against read-only policy limits before it can reach the database. This is the project's central trust boundary: LLM output remains untrusted input until a structural allow-list has approved it.
languageLesson: An SQL AST exposes statement structure for validation, which is more reliable than matching keywords in generated text and supports deny-by-default policy decisions.

title: SQLite Data Layer
description: The database layer initializes the demo schema, supplies schema context, executes bounded approved queries, and renders results. It turns the policy-approved request from Step 8 into data while keeping SQLite and connection-management concerns out of the workflow and interfaces.

title: Evidence and Evaluation
description: Structured auditing redacts SQL while retaining stable evidence of what happened, and the evaluation runner measures answer quality, safety, latency, and token use. Together they make the workflow observable and give provider or prompt changes a repeatable quality gate.

title: Continuous Quality
description: The CI workflow installs locked dependencies, checks formatting and types, runs tests and dependency auditing, builds the package, and smoke-tests the wheel. Local pre-commit hooks bring a focused subset of those protections into the developer loop before changes reach continuous integration.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions model automation as triggered workflows containing jobs and ordered steps, while pre-commit hooks provide a faster local feedback loop for compatible checks.
